exposure: Informed consent to midwifery practices and interventions during the second stage of labor
Use of warm compresses held at the perineum
outcome: Women's experiences of the second stage of labor
Experiences of clinical practices and interventions
Discomfort from interventions involving physical penetration of the genital area
Pain from interventions involving physical penetration of the genital area
cohort: The study included 2849 women who gave birth spontaneously in five Swedish maternity wards and consented to receive a follow-up questionnaire from the Oneplus trial.
finding: Informed consent, reported by less than one in five women, was associated with feelings of being safe, strong, and in control, more positive experiences of clinical practices and interventions, and less discomfort and pain.
cross-section timing: One month after giving birth spontaneously
